one_sentence: Gravitational force and sin share a structural isomorphism because both are manifestations of the same substrate operating at different measurement scales.
executive_summary: This document claims a structural isomorphism between gravitational force and sin, arguing that both follow the same mathematical architecture: an inverse-square law of attraction, binding energy requiring external input for escape, and universal pull. Key evidence includes the mapping of physical variables (mass, distance, force) to theological variables (moral mass, distance from God, sin's pull), supported by four separator tests (structural preservation, non-arbitrariness, constraint, bidirectionality) and empirical data from 28 cultures. The conclusion is that this isomorphism is Level 3 (structural), with falsification criteria (e.g., sin as repulsive force) and bidirectional predictions: civilizations with greater moral mass collapse faster, and conversion experiences show threshold effects.
short_summary: This document is a formal isomorphism paper mapping gravitational force to sin. The core structural claim is that both phenomena obey an inverse-square law of attraction with binding energy and escape velocity. Key evidence includes four separator tests (structural preservation, non-arbitrariness, constraint, bidirectionality) and empirical data from 28 cultures. This matters because it establishes a bidirectional constraint between physics and theology, enabling predictions in both domains.
